Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for the Least Costly Two-Phase Design

Source: R/ss_aipe_two_phase_cost.R
ss_aipe_two_phase_cost.Rd

Takes planning values for a two-phase design (the standard deviation of a costly target measurement, its correlation with an inexpensive proxy, and the cost of a proxy relative to a target measurement) and a desired confidence interval width for the target mean. Returns the number of labeled units \(n\), which carry both measurements, and the number of pool units \(M\), which carry the proxy, of the least costly design in whole numbers whose interval from ci_two_phase has an expected width no larger than desired. The table also gives the cost relative to measuring the target alone and the correlation the proxy must have before it can save anything.

Usage

ss_aipe_two_phase_cost(
  true_sd_Y,
  true_cor,
  width,
  cost_ratio,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

true_sd_Y

Planning value of the standard deviation of the target measurement, \(\sigma_Y\).

true_cor

Planning value of the correlation between the target and the proxy, \(\rho\). Only its absolute value matters.

width

The desired full width of the confidence interval (the upper limit minus the lower limit), in the units of the target.

cost_ratio

The cost of one proxy measurement relative to one target measurement, \(r = c_P / c_T\), a number in (0, 1).

conf_level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

Value

A data.frame (classes dmar_ss_aipe and dmar_tbl) with rows

necessary_n_labeled

the number of labeled units, \(n\); when necessary_n_pool is 0, the number of units for the target alone.

necessary_n_pool

the number of units in the pool, \(M\), every one of which carries the proxy; 0 when the design measures the target alone.

relative_cost

the cost of the returned design, \(n + rM\), over the cost of the target alone, necessary_n_target_only, both in whole numbers under the criteria above; 1 when the returned design is the target alone.

relative_cost_continuous

the same ratio for fractional sizes under the normal quantile, \((\sqrt{1 - \rho^2} + |\rho|\sqrt{r})^2\), or 1 at or below threshold_cor; reported for comparison.

expected_width

the planned full width at the returned sizes and the planning values: the left side of the two-phase inequality above, or of the target-alone inequality when the pool is 0. It is at most width.

necessary_n_target_only

the number of units the target alone needs for the same width.

threshold_cor

the absolute correlation above which the proxy lowers the cost of the fractional solution, \(2\sqrt{r}/(1 + r)\).

width, true_sd_Y, true_cor, cost_ratio, conf_level

the inputs.

Details

Estimand and interval. The quantity to be estimated is \(\mu_Y\), the population mean of the target measurement. The sampling unit is one unit of the pool: \(M\) units are drawn at random, the proxy is observed on all of them, and the target on a simple random subsample of \(n\) of them. The interval planned for is the one ci_two_phase reports for the regression estimator of double sampling, a Wald-type interval whose standard error estimates \(\sigma_Y^2(1 - \rho^2)/n + \rho^2\sigma_Y^2/M\) and whose reference distribution is t on \(n - 2\) degrees of freedom. This is a plan for the expected width, with no assurance: about half of all realized intervals are wider than width. ss_aipe_two_phase adds an assurance for a given pool.

The cost model. Every unit of the pool, the labeled ones included, costs \(c_P\) for its proxy, and each labeled unit costs \(c_T\) more for its target, so a design costs \(c_T n + c_P M\), which is \(n + rM\) in units of one target measurement. In an evaluation of a system whose outputs an automated judge labels, for example, \(c_T\) is the cost of a human assessor's label and \(c_P\) that of the judge's. The target alone on \(n\) units costs \(n\).

Which designs are admissible. A two-phase design has \(n \ge 3\) and \(M \ge n + 1\), the least ci_two_phase accepts, and meets the width when, with \(q = 1 - (1 - \mathrm{conf\_level})/2\) and \(\omega\) the desired width (width), $$2\, t_{q,\, n-2}\, \sigma_Y \left\{\frac{1 - \rho^2}{n} + \frac{\rho^2}{M}\right\}^{1/2} \le \omega,$$ the criterion ss_aipe_two_phase uses for a given pool, so that planner, given n_pool = necessary_n_pool, returns necessary_n_labeled. The left side sets the two estimates in the standard error at their planning values, which overstates the expected width slightly (see ss_aipe_two_phase). The alternative without a proxy is the t interval for one mean on the smallest \(n\) with \(2\, t_{q,\, n-1}\, c_4(n)\, \sigma_Y / \sqrt{n} \le \omega\), where \(c_4(n)\sigma_Y\) is the expected sample standard deviation under normality; this is the necessary_n_target_only row here and in ss_aipe_two_phase. Because the t quantile is part of the requirement, a design with very few labeled units is admissible only when it is wide enough to pay for its quantile (12.7 at a 95% level with 3 labeled units), and no separate minimum is imposed.

The search. For each \(n\) the smallest admissible pool follows from the inequality above, so the search is over \(n\) alone. Since \(t_{q,\, n-2}\) is at least the normal quantile \(z_q\), no design with \(n\) labeled units can cost less than \(n + r \max\{n + 1,\; b/(1 - a/n)\}\) for \(n > a\), and none exists for \(n \le a\), where \(a = (1 - \rho^2) s\) and \(b = \rho^2 s\) with \(s = (2 z_q \sigma_Y/\omega)^2\). That bound is convex in \(n\), so the function starts at its minimizer with the target alone as the design to beat, examines every \(n\) above and then below the minimizer for as long as the bound is less than the cost of the best design found, and returns that design. No design in whole numbers costs less: every \(n\) not examined has a bound at least as large as the cost returned. A two-phase design is returned only when it costs less than the target alone, and among designs of equal cost the first found is kept, so a tie with the target alone returns the target alone. The search and its bound were derived for DMAR; in 2,200 planning sets drawn at random (correlations of either sign from .02 to .999, cost ratios from .001 to .98, four confidence levels) the result equaled an exhaustive search over pairs \((n, M)\) every time.

The fractional solution, for comparison. If the sizes could be fractional and the normal quantile were used, minimizing \(n + rM\) subject to \(a/n + b/M = 1\) (a Lagrange multiplier argument) gives \(n = a + \sqrt{rab}\) and \(M = b + \sqrt{ab/r}\), at a cost of \((\sqrt{1 - \rho^2} + |\rho|\sqrt{r})^2\) times the \(s\) units the target alone would need. That factor is the relative_cost_continuous row. It is below 1 exactly when \(|\rho| > 2\sqrt{r}/(1 + r)\), the threshold_cor row; at or below that correlation the row is 1. The two sizes are in the ratio \(M/n = \sqrt{b/(ra)}\): each is proportional to its share of the variance and inversely proportional to the square root of its cost. Neyman (1938, Equations 49, 52, and 53, pp. 110–111) derived that square root rule for double sampling in which the inexpensive variable forms strata and the variance is minimized for a fixed total cost; the form here, with a regression on the proxy and the cost minimized for a fixed width, is the same allocation problem stated the other way round. For the regression estimator itself, Tamhane (1978, Equation 2.2, p. 421) gives the same ratio of the two sizes for a fixed budget, and the correlation above which double sampling is no worse than the target alone, \(\rho^2 \ge 4 c_1 c_2/(c_1 + c_2)^2\) with \(c_1\) and \(c_2\) the costs of the proxy and of the target, which is threshold_cor; the result is for a bivariate normal population with a known covariance matrix. The fractional solution is a lower bound: no design in whole numbers that meets the width costs less than relative_cost_continuous times \(s\) target measurements. The design returned costs more than that bound because sizes are whole numbers and because the interval uses the t quantile (a median of 7% more, and far more when only a few units are needed, in the 891 random planning sets above in which a two-phase design was returned).

What can happen at the edges.

  • A correlation at or below threshold_cor: the target alone is returned (necessary_n_pool is 0 and relative_cost is 1). In the random planning sets above no two-phase design was ever the least costly there.

  • A correlation above threshold_cor: the threshold is exact for fractional sizes and the normal quantile only. The target alone can still be the least costly design in whole numbers, most often when few units are needed or the correlation is a little above the threshold (376 of the 1,267 random planning sets above the threshold), and it is then returned.

  • true_cor = 0: the proxy carries no information and the target alone is returned.

  • A proxy that costs as much as the target or more (cost_ratio of 1 or more) never saves anything and is refused with an error of class dmar_cost_ratio_invalid.

  • A very wide width: the target alone needs at least 2 units, the fewest from which a standard deviation can be estimated.

  • Sizes that cannot be represented as whole numbers (above \(2^{52}\), about 4.5e15), or a search that would examine more than \(10^8\) values of \(n\): refused with an error of class dmar_two_phase_no_design. Neither arises for a width within a factor of a million of true_sd_Y.

References

Neyman, J. (1938). Contribution to the theory of sampling human populations. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 33(201), 101–116. doi:10.1080/01621459.1938.10503378

Tamhane, A. C. (1978). Inference based on regression estimator in double sampling. Biometrika, 65(2), 419–427. doi:10.1093/biomet/65.2.419

See also

ss_aipe_two_phase for the labeled units given a pool, with or without an assurance, ci_two_phase for the interval, and ss_aipe_two_phase_sensitivity to evaluate a design by simulation.

Examples

# A proxy measurement costs 1% of a target measurement. Planning values
# of 0.43 for the target's standard deviation and 0.55 for its
# correlation with the proxy; a 90% interval no wider than 0.10. The
# least costly design labels 151 units of a pool of 957 and costs 79%
# of what the 202 units of the target alone would.
ss_aipe_two_phase_cost(true_sd_Y = 0.43, true_cor = 0.55, width = 0.10,
                       cost_ratio = 0.01, conf_level = 0.90)
#>  term                     value
#>  necessary_n_labeled      151  
#>  necessary_n_pool         957  
#>  relative_cost            0.795
#>  relative_cost_continuous 0.792
#>  expected_width           0.100
#>  necessary_n_target_only  202  
#>  threshold_cor            0.198
#>  width                    0.100
#>  true_sd_Y                0.430
#>  true_cor                 0.550
#>  cost_ratio               0.010
#>  conf_level               0.900
#> 
#> Confidence level: 90%

# At 10% of the cost the same proxy no longer pays: a correlation of 0.55
# is below the threshold, and the design measures the target alone.
ss_aipe_two_phase_cost(true_sd_Y = 0.43, true_cor = 0.55, width = 0.10,
                       cost_ratio = 0.10, conf_level = 0.90)
#>  term                     value
#>  necessary_n_labeled      202  
#>  necessary_n_pool         0    
#>  relative_cost            1    
#>  relative_cost_continuous 1    
#>  expected_width           0.100
#>  necessary_n_target_only  202  
#>  threshold_cor            0.575
#>  width                    0.100
#>  true_sd_Y                0.430
#>  true_cor                 0.550
#>  cost_ratio               0.100
#>  conf_level               0.900
#> 
#> Confidence level: 90%

# A worked example in standard deviation units: a proxy that correlates
# 0.90 with the target at 5% of its cost, and a 95% interval of width
# 0.20. The design is 109 labeled units in a pool of 1011, a cost of
# 109 + 0.05 * 1011 = 159.55 target measurements against 387.
plan <- ss_aipe_two_phase_cost(true_sd_Y = 1, true_cor = 0.90, width = 0.20,
                               cost_ratio = 0.05)
plan
#>  term                     value
#>  necessary_n_labeled      109  
#>  necessary_n_pool         1011 
#>  relative_cost            0.412
#>  relative_cost_continuous 0.406
#>  expected_width           0.200
#>  necessary_n_target_only  387  
#>  threshold_cor            0.426
#>  width                    0.200
#>  true_sd_Y                1    
#>  true_cor                 0.900
#>  cost_ratio               0.050
#>  conf_level               0.950
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# The companion planner, given that pool, returns the same number of
# labeled units.
ss_aipe_two_phase(true_sd_Y = 1, true_cor = 0.90, width = 0.20, n_pool = 1011)
#>  term                    value
#>  necessary_n_labeled     109  
#>  necessary_n_target_only 387  
#>  ratio                   0.282
#>  expected_width          0.200
#>  minimum_width           0.123
#>  width                   0.200
#>  true_sd_Y               1    
#>  true_cor                0.900
#>  n_pool                  1011 
#>  conf_level              0.950
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
